title: Auto Loans: fees due and loan balance recomputed from the ledger for a catch-up installment payment
content:
# Auto Loans: fees due and loan balance recomputed from the ledger for a catch-up installment payment

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower pays the earliest past-due installment of an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account. It fixes the two balances the payment is split against. In this rule, **Principal** means the unpaid loan balance, and a payment's **Principal Portion** is the part of that payment applied to it.

## Clauses

1. **Fees due** are recomputed from the loan's ledger as the total of every fee entry on the loan, less the total of every fee settlement, less the total of every fee waiver, rounded to the cent. Fee entries include late charges, extension fees, returned payment fees and settlement reversals.
2. **Principal** is recomputed from the loan's ledger as the disbursement amount, less the Principal Portion of every payment on the loan, plus the amount of every payment reversal, rounded to the cent.

## Ledger view

| Ledger entry | Effect on fees due | Effect on Principal |
|---|---|---|
| Disbursement at funding | none | sets the starting figure |
| Fee of any kind | adds its amount | none |
| Fee settlement | takes its amount off | none |
| Fee waiver | takes its amount off | none |
| Payment | none directly | takes its Principal Portion off |
| Payment reversal | none directly | adds its amount back |

## Worked case (hypothetical ledger)

- Disbursement 24000.00; Principal Portions of all payments 6210.55; one payment reversal of 314.63. Principal: 24000.00 less 6210.55 plus 314.63, that is 18104.08.
- Fees assessed 25.00, 18.08 and 25.00, totalling 68.08; fee settlements 25.00; fee waivers 18.08. Fees due: 68.08 less 25.00 less 18.08, that is 25.00.

## Contrast

**Wrong reading:** "a returned payment still reduces the loan balance because its Principal Portion is on the ledger." **Correct basis:** the payment reversal's amount is added back, so the returned payment no longer reduces Principal.

**Wrong reading:** "a waived fee is still owed until it is paid." **Correct basis:** every fee waiver is taken off the fees due.
